iconicAnchor.label: Contemporary Poetry Society of America chapbooks
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Poets, small presses, and chapbook designers
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The documented series shows the chapbook as a compact, intentionally designed container whose typography, material choices, covers, and page pacing remain subordinate to the poem.

sources.title: A Look Inside the Poetry Society of America's Chapbook Series
supports: The pictured series demonstrates varied but intentional small-format production and cover systems.
The examples support treating material scale and page sequence as part of the poetic reading experience.

sources.title: And what do I love in loving thee?
supports: The discussion connects chapbook design decisions to the character of the poems rather than a fixed decorative system.
It supports close attention to typography, binding, paper, and the physical intimacy of a short publication.

bundledReferenceRationale: The open small-format verse spread is an excellent lead. Sparse lineation, generous white space, understated typography, page numbers, and intimate scale remain legible and unmistakably chapbook-like. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/poetry-chapbook/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
